Fixed, but the bead's premise was wrong and is worth recording. It assumed vord's migrations need the same re-entrancy test as vord-internal's. They do not: InitialMigration has exactly two guarded statements in 1028 lines (the hangfire schema, plus an unreachable pg_trgm block) and InitialMigration2 has none, because both are fresh-install-only by documented policy and freeze at first ship. The sibling's delete-version-row-and-reapply template cannot execute here; it throws 42P07 on the second Create.Table. The real defect underneath was genuine and is fixed: the old test asserted VersionInfo row counts and would have passed with every guard deleted. It now exercises the one reachable guard with a proven-discriminating assertion, asserts the DELETE affected exactly one row so version drift fails loud rather than vacuously, and the class remark no longer claims an idempotency invariant this repo does not hold. pg_trgm guards remain untested and deliberately so: FluentMigrator wraps each migration in a transaction, so no database can exist in the half-applied state those guards imagine.

Fixed by converting PostgresFixture to one shared container with a per-fixture database; all 16 test classes untouched. Baseline reproduced the flake (1 of 3 runs); 14 green runs since, peak concurrent containers 1, run time 33-38s down to 24-31s. The port-publication race is eliminated structurally, not just statistically: the mechanism needs two containers publishing concurrently and the measured peak is 1.

Two hazards the shared cluster introduced were found and closed. AdvisoryLockLivenessLiveTests terminated backends via cluster-wide pg_stat_activity/pg_locks and would have killed another class's lock holders; scoped to current_database(). And consolidating onto one container put the suite at 91 backends against a default limit of 100 - measured, not theoretical - so max_connections is now 800 with a per-pool cap of 20. Re-measuring at 93 backends after raising the cap confirmed the cap was never the binding constraint; max_connections alone fixed the exhaustion risk.

Advisory locks were checked and are NOT a cross-class hazard: the lock tag includes MyDatabaseId, so bigint advisory locks in different databases never conflict. The pg_locks and pg_stat_activity views are cluster-wide, the locks are not.

Untested: the container start-failure path (dispose-on-failure and teardown fault-skip are reviewed-correct but never exercised). RedisFixture keeps the old pattern, filed as vord-jtj.

Not a bug — invalid on verification. countPhysicalCoresFromData returning 0 is a documented sentinel, not the reported value: both call sites already apply the exact fallback that was proposed as the fix. slowtick.go:207-213 seeds physicalCores = runtime.NumCPU() and overrides only when count > 0 (this is what fills cpu_physical_cores); slowtick.go:322-328 does the same for the cpu-info payload. runtime.NumCPU() is always >= 1, so 0 can never reach the wire. TestCountPhysicalCoresARM (cpuinfo_test.go:222-228) already covers the no-topology case and asserts 0 deliberately as the helper contract.
